title: Knowledge base
description: What an extension's program may ask of the knowledge base directly (docs/extensions/extensions.md "Knowledge base RPC"): kb.list, kb.recent, kb.get, kb.day, kb.search, kb.owner (permission kb.read), kb.update and kb.put_recording (kb.write), and the events event.kb.changed / event.kb.forgotten. An extension's kb.update is attributed to it: it may not touch what the user or another extension holds (conflict), and it holds the locked fields it writes (docs/assistant/knowledge.md "Who holds a field"). Params are strict: no contribution, and an unknown field is invalid_params. A connector hands the knowledge base its conversations, items and posts through the connector calls instead (connector.schema.json). Plugin-side: only the hub and the program speak it.

KBImportCheckpointParams.description: The host selects the provider, source, account and chat for this import.

KBImportState.description: The host importer’s committed state for the selected chat.

KBErrorCode.description: error.code of a knowledge-base call besides permission_denied (data {scope}, the one missing): invalid_params, not_found, assistant_offline (the manager is away), kb_unavailable (not open yet), conflict (kb.update touches fields the user or another extension holds; data KBConflict, nothing was written). assistant_offline and kb_unavailable are worth trying again; conflict is for the user to decide. deleted: kb.put_recording of a recording the user deleted, which is not made again.

KBConflict.description: The data of a conflict error: field → who holds it (user, or ext:<extension id>); a linked entity's field is <kind>/<id>.<field>.

KBEvidence.description: What a written value rests on: a chat's day (kb.day) and optionally the line n there.

day.description: YYYY-MM-DD in the knowledge base's time zone.

n.description: 1-based line in that day's file (kb.day's n).

KBProvenance.description: An entry of an entity's meta.provenance (kb.get): which extension holds that locked field, since when, from what. A locked field without one is the user's.

KBHandle.description: An identity clue: kind (phone, email, a source's user id kind…) and the raw value.

KBListParams.description: kb.list: one kind's entities, ranked; pages are not a snapshot (deduplicate, read again when needed).

since.description: An RFC 3339 time: only entities updated at or after it (a chat: its last message).

next_offset.description: Where the next page starts; none at the end.

relevance.description: 0–100: how much it concerns the owner.

extra.description: A project's short / long · status, a chat's dm / group…

source.description: A chat's source (lark, mail, wechat, github…); a document's, meeting's or event's connector (#8872).

recording_kind.description: A recording's kind: meeting, note or day (#8870); absent on other kinds and from an older hub.

meeting_id.description: A recording's imported meeting: the id of the meetings item it overlaps, as the meetings list has it (#8872); absent on other kinds, before a match and from an older hub.

paused.description: A recording whose stored state is in flight (an upload not complete, minutes or a day recap pending, a hub transcription not final) while nothing can settle it: module_off when the recording module is off. Derived when read, never stored; absent otherwise and from an older hub.

project_mode.description: Reference-only for a project that stores pointers. Omitted means full.

KBRecentParams.description: kb.recent (kb.read): what came in from every source in [since, until), newest first, across kinds: one feed for a curation pass. Read a chat's text with kb.day, anything else with kb.get.

until.description: An RFC 3339 time; none is now.

kinds.description: None is chats, docs, meetings, events and recordings.

KBGetParams.description: kb.get: one entity, with its most recent messages (recent_chars, none is 12000; 0 leaves them out). Live agents are not in it.

path.description: Where it is on the manager's machine, for its own file tools.

meta.description: The entity's own fields (meta.json). For people, status is active, ignored or self; absent or empty means active. Status uses the same locked_fields and provenance as other corrected fields.

removed.description: The links the user removed by hand (meta's excluded), named as links are; automatic organizing and extensions leave them out until the user links them again (docs/assistant/knowledge.md "Removed links").

minutes.description: A recording's meeting minutes, once written (docs/assistant/meeting-minutes.md); kept as the hub sends them.

recap.description: An all-day recording's day recap, once written (docs/assistant/day-recap.md); kept as the hub sends them.

speakers.description: A hub-transcribed meeting's speaker list and timeline (docs/assistant/meeting-minutes.md "Speakers (#17674)"); absent when the meeting has no speaker timeline.

profiles.description: A person's profiles by writer ("user", "ext:<id>"), as written; summary shows them too (docs/assistant/knowledge.md "Person profiles").

paused.description: A recording's in-flight state that nothing can settle, as KBEntry.paused: module_off when the recording module is off. Derived when read, never stored.

project_mode.description: Reference-only for a project that stores pointers. Omitted means full.

KBSpeakerState.description: Speaker separation state of a hub-transcribed meeting.

KBSpeakerID.description: Hub-assigned speaker identifier within a meeting (s1, s2, ...).

KBSpeakerTurn.description: One speaking interval encoded as a 3-element JSON tuple [start, end, speaker_id].

KBDetailSpeakers.description: A hub-transcribed meeting's speaker list and timeline on detail.speakers (docs/assistant/meeting-minutes.md "Speakers (#17674)").

id.description: Canonical source identity shared across project views.

delivery_state.description: State observed at the source, such as merged.

environment_verification.description: Unverified when only source delivery facts are available.

writer.description: Omitted when historical authorship is unknown.

uncovered_evidence_count.description: Omitted when the gap cannot be counted.

timeline_truncated.description: True if earlier timeline entries were outside this refresh window.

KBPersonProfile.description: One writer's profile of a person, its four parts kept apart. Every item says where it comes from; at most 30 items a part, and 8000 bytes as summary.md shows it.

facts.description: Their role, what they are in charge of, how they relate to the user.

views.description: The user's own words about them, quoted.

inferences.description: Inferred, never stated: each needs its basis. Shown as only a hint.

commitments.description: Promises and to-dos between the user and them, either way.

basis.description: Inferences only (required there): what it rests on.

sources.description: Where it comes from: a knowledge-base path (chats/<id>/messages/<day>.md, recordings/<id>), a URL, or "user" for the user's own word.

owes.description: user: the user owes it to them; them: they owe it to the user.

KBIgnoredField.description: A field an update carried that its kind does not use: not applied, and why.

KBTopicPoint.description: One knowledge point of a topic, under up to two levels of subtopics (path).

why.description: A decision's reason, a pitfall's cause.

when.description: YYYY-MM-DD: when it was last confirmed.

KBTopicSource.description: An entry a knowledge point came from.

KBMomentRef.description: A feed post linked to a project.

note.description: How it bears on the project.

KBRecordingSegment.description: A recording's transcript segment, in seconds from its start.

n.description: An all-day recording's line number: the segment's 1-based position in its uploads (docs/assistant/day-recap.md); absent on other recordings.

source.description: Whose text the segment is in a meeting transcribed on the hub (docs/assistant/meeting-minutes.md "The transcript of record"): hub or device; absent means device.

echo.description: The line is Persona's own answer as the meeting's microphone heard it (docs/assistant/meeting-minutes.md "Persona's echo"): kept in the transcript but not what the meeting said, so leave it out of anything read as the meeting's words; absent (false) on every other line.

speaker.description: Canonical speaker id ("s1", "s2", ...) assigned by the hub on read when a speaker timeline exists (docs/assistant/meeting-minutes.md "Speakers (#17674)"); absent otherwise.

speaker_unsure.description: True when the speaker label is uncertain or the meeting's separation quality is low (docs/assistant/meeting-minutes.md "Speakers (#17674)"); absent (false) otherwise.

KBDayParams.description: kb.day: a chat's messages of one day in the knowledge base's time zone.

day.description: YYYY-MM-DD, a real date (the hub refuses 2026-13-45).

KBDayResult.description: prev and next are the days before and after that have messages (empty: none).

sent_origin.description: available means ledger matching ran, not that unmarked messages are human-authored. missing_scope requires sent.read; unavailable means the service cannot provide provenance. Older hosts omit this field: treat absence as unavailable.

n.description: The message's first line in the day's file, from 1.

sent_by.description: Present only for a unique match in the sent-as-user ledger, with sent.read.

recalled_at.description: When this matched send was recalled; the archive may still contain its text.

KBSearchParams.description: kb.search: lines that match, messages too unless messages is false.

query.description: Not only spaces (the hub refuses that).

KBUpdateParams.description: kb.update: kind and id, and the fields to change (the knowledge base's update API, plus pinned, lock and the remove_* lists). A field left out is kept; the other lists add to what is there. Protected fields and history limits: docs/assistant/knowledge.md.

pinned.description: Confirmed facts automatic writes cannot replace; an empty string clears them.

lock.description: Whether an importance / relevance given here is kept from automatic tagging (default true).

status.description: People: active, ignored or self; other values are rejected by kb.update. Projects: active, paused, done or ignored. Omitted or empty keeps the current status; active restores a person.

tags.description: Replaces the tags; an empty list clears them, none keeps them.

log.description: A project's: a line appended to its timeline.

merge_into.description: Refused (conflict) when the user or another extension holds anything on the project folded away; no before.

profile.description: People only: this extension's own profile of the person, replacing the one it wrote before (one with no items removes it). Nobody else's profile, nor pinned or note, is touched; before.profile is the one replaced. A profile breaking a rule is invalid_params and nothing is written.

evidence.description: Kept as the provenance of the fields this write holds.

unlock.description: Fields this extension holds, handed back to the built-in pipeline; unlocking pinned clears it.

before.description: The previous value of each field written (null when unset; summary is the old text, profile this extension's own profile before), for the extension's own undo.

ignored.description: Fields the update carried that its kind does not use (a person's summary and log, for one), and links to make that the user removed: not applied, each with why.

KBRecordingID.description: A recording's UUID, picked by the extension so a retry lands on the same recording.

KBMinutesActionID.description: An action item's id, picked by the extension and stable across writes.

KBTodoID.description: A to-do's id, set by the hub when the user makes a to-do of an action item.

KBRecordingMeetingKind.description: Whether a recording's meeting is a calendar item (events) or an imported meeting (meetings).

KBRecordingMeetingID.description: A calendar item's or imported meeting's id in the knowledge base.

KBPutRecordingParams.description: kb.put_recording (kb.write): create or update the extension's own recording with its minutes and, optionally, its transcript (docs/extensions/extensions.md "Writing recordings and minutes"). It is the extension's: no other extension may write it, and no extension a recording the phone uploaded (permission_denied). The same params again change nothing; a recording the user deleted is not made again (deleted). A recording with minutes is kept past recording_days, its minutes until minutes_days.

id.description: A UUID the extension picks; one derived from its own source id makes a retry land on the same recording.

ended_at.description: An RFC 3339 time, not before started_at.

transcript.description: Optional; n, source, echo, speaker and speaker_unsure are the hub's and are dropped. Without minutes, the hub makes minutes of it when the recording module is on.

projects.description: Slugs of existing projects to link it to; a later write never removes a link.

KBRecordingMinutes.description: The minutes the extension wrote, stored as minutes.json and minutes.md. The hub sets version, revision, generated_at, when, start and end. Minutes or a transcript is required.

language.description: An i18n code: what the minutes are written in.

markdown.description: The minutes as Markdown: minutes.md, what searches and kb.get read. Required, not blank.

KBMinutesItem.description: A decision or an open question of the minutes.

KBMinutesPoint.description: A point discussed; who only when the source names the person.

KBMinutesAction.description: An action item. id is the extension's, stable across writes (at most 64 characters): a to-do the user made of it stays on it.

due_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, when by is one date.

todo_id.description: The hub's: the to-do made of it.

KBRecordingMeeting.description: The calendar item (events) or imported meeting (meetings) the recording was; it must exist.

revision.description: The hub's revision of the recording: 1 when created, one more for each write that changed it.

unchanged.description: The write was the same as the last one; nothing was written.

KBOwner.description: kb.owner: the user's name, aliases and identities across sources (raw only through this explicit read).

KBChangedEvent.description: event.kb.changed: an entity changed (what: which part). Read it again if it matters.

KBForgottenEvent.description: event.kb.forgotten: a source's data was removed from the knowledge base.
